I'm trying to create a rule for stopping diagonal movement when either coordinate is one away from a marker. Then, I need to continue along the other axis until I reach the distance of one away. For my testing, I’m considering coordinates like (1,4) and (13,12), moving diagonally down-right until I hit column 11 and then continuing vertically down. I need to define color coordinates and eventually produce a grid for the program.

{
 "content": "def transform(grid):
    out=[row[:] for row in grid]
    one=next(((r,c) for r,row in enumerate(grid) for c,v in enumerate(row) if v==1),None)
    two=next(((r,c) for r,row in enumerate(grid) for c,v in enumerate(row) if v==2),None)
    if one is None or two is None:return out
    r,c=one; tr,tc=two
    dr=1 if tr>r else -1
    dc=1 if tc>c else -1
    # Travel diagonally until adjacent to either coordinate of the target.
    while abs(tr-r)>1 and abs(tc-c)>1:
        nr,nc=r+dr,c+dc
        if not (0<=nr<len(grid) and 0<=nc<len(grid[0])): break
        r,c=nr,nc
        if (r,c)!=two: out[r][c]=3
    # Continue straight along the remaining coordinate, stopping adjacent to target.
    if abs(tr-r)>1:
        while abs(tr-r)>1:
            r+=dr
            if (r,c)!=two:out[r][c]=3
    elif abs(tc-c)>1:
        while abs(tc-c)>1:
            c+=dc
            if (r,c)!=two:out[r][c]=3
    return out
"
